channel.title: NRBC Compliance Brief
channel.description: A daily morning brief from New Realm Brewing on alcohol and hemp/THC regulation — TTB and state actions, hemp THC beverage rules, tariffs, court decisions and enforcement. Federal and all 50 states.

item.title: Illinois sets hemp retailer rules for Nov. 12 — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 75 (Oct 27, 2026)
item.description: Illinois Revenue Department sets retailer compliance steps for the Nov. 12 hemp overhaul. Also: OMB clears streamlined USDA hemp production survey; Massachusetts House leader defends state-run liquor licensing after auditor urges overhaul

item.title: House bill offers brewers spent-grain tax credit — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 74 (Oct 26, 2026)
item.description: Bipartisan House bill would give brewers an excise tax credit for donated spent grain. Also: Booker presses DEA on employee-conviction rules for registering dispensaries; New Jersey hemp-drink extension is one Assembly vote from passage

item.title: Texas hemp groups sue over THCA rule, fees — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 73 (Oct 25, 2026)
item.description: Texas hemp groups sue DSHS over THCA rule and sharply higher license fees. Also: UPS to require THC testing documentation on hemp shipments starting Dec. 11; Virginia Senate finance chair indicted on federal marijuana and racketeering charges

item.title: DEA registration staffing rules draw Senate criticism — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 72 (Oct 24, 2026)
item.description: DEA registration rules force staffing choices at marijuana retailers seeking Schedule III protections. Also: Oklahoma's top medical marijuana regulator steps down; compliance chief named interim director; Minnesota opens $10.9 million CanRenew grant round; businesses among eligible applicants

item.title: New Jersey Senate votes to extend hemp-drink sales — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 71 (Oct 23, 2026)
item.description: New Jersey Senate votes 37–0 to extend hemp-beverage sales window and tie it to the federal timeline. Also: DEA judge declines to reopen marijuana rescheduling hearing, sets final briefing dates; Virginia Senate finance chair indicted on federal marijuana and racketeering charges

item.title: Rhode Island lets hemp sellers quarantine over-limit stock — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 70 (Oct 22, 2026)
item.description: Rhode Island lets hemp businesses quarantine over-limit THC inventory instead of destroying it. Also: DEA opposes rescheduling opponents' bid to reopen marijuana hearing over GAO report; Hemp drink maker launches campaign sending six-packs to Congress ahead of federal THC limit

item.title: Delaware THC beverage law takes effect — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 69 (Oct 21, 2026)
item.description: Delaware’s THC beverage law takes effect today, opening sales at package stores and dispensaries. Also: THC drink maker sends six-packs to members of Congress as federal limits approach; Colorado audit finds gaps in marijuana product-testing oversight

item.title: Supreme Court to review federal home-distilling ban — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 68 (Oct 20, 2026)
item.description: Supreme Court agrees to review the 1868 federal ban on home distilling. Also: NORML asks Sixth Circuit to reconsider ruling that cannabis contracts are unenforceable; THC drink maker launches campaign to send six-packs to members of Congress

item.title: Hemp beverage group sees possible federal fix — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 67 (Oct 19, 2026)
item.description: Hemp beverage trade group "optimistic" a federal solution emerges before the ban, but says "miniature prohibition" is possible. Also: Trade court certifies nationwide importer class for IEEPA tariff refunds; Coors Distributing and Constellation square off in court over terminated distribution rights

item.title: Kentucky hemp industry seeks lower license fees — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 66 (Oct 18, 2026)
item.description: Kentucky hemp industry asks lawmakers to cut license fees and restore on-premises hemp beverage sales ahead of the 2027 session. Also: Rep. Barr details proposed federal hemp framework: age limits, testing, per-serving potency caps, packaging limits and dual taxes; Kentucky medical cannabis dispensa

item.title: Massachusetts lawmakers oppose cannabis-sales repeal measure — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 65 (Oct 17, 2026)
item.description: 62 Massachusetts lawmakers announce opposition to Question 8, the ballot measure that would repeal commercial cannabis sales. Also: Undisclosed-donor group runs ad against Sen. Sheehy's push to keep hemp THC products legal; Sheehy-Klobuchar bill in the works; Administration asks Supreme Court to dec

item.title: Illinois to enforce hemp THC limits Nov. 12 — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 64 (Oct 16, 2026)
item.description: Illinois will enforce its 0.4 mg hemp THC cap Nov. 12, despite the federal delay to Dec. 11. Also: DEA judge orders agency response by Oct. 21 in rescheduling case; proceedings stay paused; New Jersey committees advance bills tying hemp-beverage sales deadline to the federal Dec. 11 date

item.title: Georgia retailers brace for federal hemp THC limits — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 63 (Oct 15, 2026)
item.description: Georgia retailers prepare to pull hemp THC products ahead of the Dec. 11 federal limits. Also: What changes Nov. 12 versus Dec. 11 under the federal hemp law; At NBWA's convention, distributor leaders press for regulatory clarity amid category convergence

item.title: Supreme Court declines Ohio wine-shipping case — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 62 (Oct 14, 2026)
item.description: Supreme Court declines to review Ohio wine-shipping case, leaving retailer DTC ruling in place. Also: DEA defers on adding GAO report to rescheduling record but opposes a new round of briefing; Massachusetts auditor recommends ending the state's on-premises liquor-license quota

item.title: North Carolina braces for federal hemp THC limits — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 61 (Oct 13, 2026)
item.description: North Carolina’s $3 billion hemp industry prepares for the federal THC limits. Also: Spirits council asks administration to drop remaining 10% tariff on EU cognac and liqueurs; Washington opens public comments through Dec. 4 on medical-market certification rule

item.title: Connecticut nets $2 million unlicensed-THC distribution settlement — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 60 (Oct 12, 2026)
item.description: Connecticut reaches $2 million settlement with wholesaler over unlicensed THC product distribution. Also: Consumer group asks Congress to let the Dec. 11 hemp-THC deadline take effect; Arkansas Supreme Court: Kirkland Signature beverages are one brand, must use a single wholesaler

item.title: Rhode Island readies updated hemp-beverage guidance — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 59 (Oct 11, 2026)
item.description: Rhode Island regulators to issue updated hemp guidance as the Dec. 11 federal THC limit nears. Also: Marijuana Policy Project asks Congress to halt the hemp THC ban and adopt a regulatory framework; New Jersey Senate president files bill tying the state hemp-beverage deadline to the federal date

item.title: DOJ, challengers set rescheduling appeal timeline — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 58 (Oct 10, 2026)
item.description: Justice Department and challengers propose briefing timeline in marijuana rescheduling appeal. Also: Rep. Mast calls for ‘across-the-board’ review of federal drug scheduling; Sierra Nevada terminates Coors Distributing Co., shifting Denver-area rights to Reyes

item.title: Massachusetts senators to vote against cannabis retail repeal — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 57 (Oct 9, 2026)
item.description: Massachusetts senators say they will vote against ballot measure ending retail cannabis sales. Also: Washington regulators open rulemaking to help licensees document medical-market status for federal registration; Missouri jury awards $10 million in cannabis license ownership dispute as state drafts

item.title: State regulators press DEA for rescheduling guidance — NRBC Compliance Brief Vol. 1, Ed. 56 (Oct 8, 2026)
item.description: State regulators say DEA has not answered their marijuana rescheduling questions. Also: DEA denies MedPharm's bulk marijuana manufacturing registration, citing unregistered production; Ohio package-size, potency and purchase rules now in effect for marijuana products
